# Base-only allocation/disposal control, with no bend-kit imports.
import Base

type Blob is Type:
  Blob{size: U32, buffer: Array<U32>}

type Item is Type:
  Item{blob: Blob}

def build(count: Nat, acc: List<&1, Item>) -> List<&1, Item>:
  match count:
    case 0n:
      acc
    case 1n+rest:
      build(rest, Item{Blob{1, Array.new(U32, 0n, 48)}} <> acc)

def elapsed(label: String, start: Nat) -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    end : Nat <- IO.now()
    IO.print(label ++ " " ++ Nat.show((end - start : Nat)))

def erased(value: List<&1, Item>, start: Nat) -> IO(Unit):
  elapsed("DISPOSE_MS", start)

def retained(value: List<&1, Item>, +output: Chan(List<&1, Item>), start: Nat) -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    sent : Bool <- Chan.send(List<&1, Item>, output, value)
    elapsed("BUILD_MS", start)
    disposal : Nat <- IO.now()
    received : List<&1, Item> <- IO.join(List<&1, Item>, output)
    erased(received, disposal)

def measure(nodes: Nat) -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    output0 : Chan(List<&1, Item>) <- Chan.new(List<&1, Item>, 1)
    +output : Chan(List<&1, Item>) = output0
    start : Nat <- IO.now()
    retained(build(nodes, Nil{}), output, start)

def repeat(count: Nat, +nodes: Nat) -> IO(Unit):
  match count:
    case 0n:
      IO.print("DONE")
    case 1n+rest:
      do IO<Unit>:
        measure(nodes)
        repeat(rest, nodes)

def load(count: Nat, +holds: Chan(Array<U32>)) -> IO(Unit):
  match count:
    case 0n:
      IO.pure(Unit, Unit{})
    case 1n+rest:
      do IO<Unit>:
        sent : Bool <- Chan.send(Array<U32>, holds, Array.new(U32, 18n, 0))
        load(rest, holds)

def clear(count: Nat, +holds: Chan(Array<U32>)) -> IO(Unit):
  match count:
    case 0n:
      IO.pure(Unit, Unit{})
    case 1n+rest:
      do IO<Unit>:
        array : Array<U32> <- IO.join(Array<U32>, holds)
        clear(rest, holds)

def start(+held: U32, nodes: U32, count: U32) -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    holds0 : Chan(Array<U32>) <- Chan.new(Array<U32>, (held + 1 : U32))
    +holds : Chan(Array<U32>) = holds0
    load(U32.to_nat(held), holds)
    IO.print("LOADED")
    repeat(U32.to_nat(count), U32.to_nat(nodes))
    clear(U32.to_nat(held), holds)

def numbers(held: Maybe<&2, U32>, nodes: Maybe<&2, U32>, count: Maybe<&2, U32>) -> IO(Unit):
  match held nodes count:
    case Some{h} Some{n} Some{c}:
      start(h, n, c)
    case _ _ _:
      IO.die(Unit, 1, "invalid argument")

def args(values: List<&1, String>) -> IO(Unit):
  match values:
    case program <> held <> nodes <> count <> Nil{}:
      numbers(U32.read(held), U32.read(nodes), U32.read(count))
    case _:
      IO.die(Unit, 1, "expected held arrays, node count, repeats")

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    values : List<&1, String> <- IO.args()
    args(values)

# Base-only allocation/disposal control, with no bend-kit imports.
import Base

type Blob is Type:
  Blob{size: U32, buffer: Array<U32>}

type Item is Type:
  Item{blob: Blob}

def build(count: Nat, acc: List<&1, Item>) -> List<&1, Item>:
  match count:
    case 0n:
      acc
    case 1n+rest:
      build(rest, Item{Blob{1, Array.new(U32, 0n, 48)}} <> acc)

def elapsed(label: String, start: Nat) -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    end : Nat <- IO.now()
    IO.print(label ++ " " ++ Nat.show((end - start : Nat)))

def erase(value: List<&1, Item>) -> Unit:
  match value:
    case Nil{}:
      Unit{}
    case Con{Item{Blob{size, buffer}}, rest}:
      erase(rest)

def after_erase(value: Unit, start: Nat) -> IO(Unit):
  elapsed("DISPOSE_MS", start)

def erased(value: List<&1, Item>, start: Nat) -> IO(Unit):
  after_erase(erase(value), start)

def retained(value: List<&1, Item>, +output: Chan(List<&1, Item>), start: Nat) -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    sent : Bool <- Chan.send(List<&1, Item>, output, value)
    elapsed("BUILD_MS", start)
    disposal : Nat <- IO.now()
    received : List<&1, Item> <- IO.join(List<&1, Item>, output)
    erased(received, disposal)

def measure(nodes: Nat) -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    output0 : Chan(List<&1, Item>) <- Chan.new(List<&1, Item>, 1)
    +output : Chan(List<&1, Item>) = output0
    start : Nat <- IO.now()
    retained(build(nodes, Nil{}), output, start)

def repeat(count: Nat, +nodes: Nat) -> IO(Unit):
  match count:
    case 0n:
      IO.print("DONE")
    case 1n+rest:
      do IO<Unit>:
        measure(nodes)
        repeat(rest, nodes)

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  repeat(24n, U32.to_nat(524283))

# Base-only allocation/disposal control, with no bend-kit imports.
import Base

type Blob is Type:
  Blob{size: U32, buffer: Array<U32>}

type Item is Type:
  Item{blob: Blob}

def build(count: Nat, acc: List<&1, Item>) -> List<&1, Item>:
  match count:
    case 0n:
      acc
    case 1n+rest:
      build(rest, Item{Blob{1, Array.new(U32, 0n, 48)}} <> acc)

def elapsed(label: String, start: Nat) -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    end : Nat <- IO.now()
    IO.print(label ++ " " ++ Nat.show((end - start : Nat)))

def erased(value: List<&1, Item>, start: Nat) -> IO(Unit):
  elapsed("DISPOSE_MS", start)

def retained(value: List<&1, Item>, +output: Chan(List<&1, Item>), start: Nat) -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    sent : Bool <- Chan.send(List<&1, Item>, output, value)
    elapsed("BUILD_MS", start)
    disposal : Nat <- IO.now()
    received : List<&1, Item> <- IO.join(List<&1, Item>, output)
    erased(received, disposal)

def measure(nodes: Nat) -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    output0 : Chan(List<&1, Item>) <- Chan.new(List<&1, Item>, 1)
    +output : Chan(List<&1, Item>) = output0
    start : Nat <- IO.now()
    retained(build(nodes, Nil{}), output, start)

def repeat(count: Nat, +nodes: Nat) -> IO(Unit):
  match count:
    case 0n:
      IO.print("DONE")
    case 1n+rest:
      do IO<Unit>:
        measure(nodes)
        repeat(rest, nodes)

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  repeat(24n, U32.to_nat(524283))

# Observe bounded JSON batches beside ordinary HTTP and a real timed socket read.
import Base
import ./json_progress_probe.bend as JsonProgress
import ./json_disposal_control.bend as JsonDisposal
import ./interface_check.bend as Registry
import ../http/http.bend as Http
import ../http/context_probe.bend as Transport
import bend-kit-time@0.1.0.0/time.bend as Time

type Context is Data:
  Context{mode: String, ready: Chan(Unit), go: Chan(Unit)}

def work(mode: String, body: Http.Body, started: Time.Duration) -> IO(Http.Res):
  match mode:
    case "yield":
      do IO<Http.Res>:
        IO.sleep(500)
        JsonProgress.result(True{}, started)
    case "json-dispose":
      JsonDisposal.work(body, started)
    case _:
      JsonProgress.work("json", body, started)

def run_work(context: Context, body: Http.Body) -> IO(Http.Res):
  Context{mode, ready, go} = context
  do IO<Http.Res>:
    bodies0 : Chan(Http.Body) <- Chan.new(Http.Body, 1)
    +bodies : Chan(Http.Body) = bodies0
    queued : Bool <- Chan.send(Http.Body, bodies, body)
    Registry.require(queued, "body queue closed")
    IO.print("CPU_ARMED")
    armed : Bool <- Chan.send(Unit, ready, Unit{})
    Registry.require(armed, "ready queue closed")
    IO.join(Unit, go)
    IO.print("CPU_BEGIN")
    IO.sleep(1)
    started : Time.Duration <- Time.mono()
    received : Http.Body <- IO.join(Http.Body, bodies)
    work(mode, received, started)

def handler(context: Context, request: Http.Req) -> IO(Http.Res):
  Http.Req{method, path, headers, body} = request
  match path:
    case "/cpu":
      run_work(context, body)
    case _:
      do IO<Http.Res>:
        IO.print("ORDINARY_HANDLED")
        return Http.Res{200, Http.empty(), Http.from_string("ok")}

  match count:
    case 0n:
      IO.pure(Unit, Unit{})

      do IO<Unit>:
        IO.join(Unit, ready)
        wait_ready(rest, ready)

  match count:
    case 0n:
      IO.pure(Unit, Unit{})
    case 1n+rest:
      do IO<Unit>:
        sent : Bool <- Chan.send(Unit, go, Unit{})
        Registry.require(sent, "release queue closed")
        release(rest, go)

def start(mode: String, +count: Nat, +ready: Chan(Unit), +go: Chan(Unit), timer: Chan(Unit), setup: Listener & Chan(Unit)) -> IO(Unit):
  (listener, deadline_done) = setup
  do IO<Unit>:
    requests : List<Chan(Unit)> <- Transport.accept(~Context, ~handler, Nat.add(count, 1n), Context{mode, ready, go}, 1048576n, listener)
    wait_ready(count, ready)
    IO.print("BATCH_ARMED")
    timer_ready : Bool <- Chan.send(Unit, timer, Unit{})
    Registry.require(timer_ready, "timer queue closed")
    IO.sleep(50)
    release(count, go)
    Transport.join(requests)
    IO.join(Unit, deadline_done)
    IO.print("SERVER_DONE")

def serve(mode: String, +count: U32, port: U32) -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    Registry.require(U32.is_gt(count, 0) && U32.is_le(count, 126), "invalid batch count")
    ready0 : Chan(Unit) <- Chan.new(Unit, count)
    go0 : Chan(Unit) <- Chan.new(Unit, count)
    timer0 : Chan(Unit) <- Chan.new(Unit, 1)
    +ready : Chan(Unit) = ready0
    +go : Chan(Unit) = go0
    +timer : Chan(Unit) = timer0
    listener : Listener <- IO.try(Listener, TCP.listen("127.0.0.1", port))
    IO.print("READY")
    first : Listener & Result<&1, &1, U32 & String, Socket> <- TCP.accept(listener)
    setup : Listener & Chan(Unit) <- JsonProgress.accepted(first, timer)
    start(mode, U32.to_nat(count), ready, go, timer, setup)

def numbers(mode: String, count: Maybe<&2, U32>, port: Maybe<&2, U32>) -> IO(Unit):
  match count:
    case None{}:
      IO.die(Unit, 1, "invalid count")
    case Some{n}:
      match port:
        case None{}:
          IO.die(Unit, 1, "invalid port")
        case Some{p}:
          serve(mode, n, p)

def args(values: List<&1, String>) -> IO(Unit):
  match values:
    case program <> mode <> count <> port <> Nil{}:
      numbers(mode, U32.read(count), U32.read(port))
    case _:
      IO.die(Unit, 1, "usage: json_aggregate_probe <json|yield> <count> <port>")

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    values : List<&1, String> <- IO.args()
    args(values)

conclusions.native: Base-only wrapped-list automatic erasure causes progressive allocation/disposal slowdown; explicit structural disposal eliminates this effect in the minimal control. Specific allocator locality mechanism not established.
conclusions.javascript: Dense parsing dominated measured stage; whole-process profile has List.reverse, Bytes.peek, numeric finalization and array_new hotspots. Disposal stage is not GC time and does not prove free reclamation.
conclusions.live_intervention: Fixture-only explicit disposal retains exact behavior in six socket trials and reduces 126-request native median to 3.702 seconds, but does not make event-loop scheduling responsive.
conclusions.limitations: No general JSON disposal API or production remedy; targeted fixture intervention is not a fix. Stage isolation forces result retention and changes compiler optimization opportunity. Native profile fractions apply only to isolated probe.
